pivot: Does the frontier lab implicated in the Stage-2 reversal still have its own branded or self-run deployment pending in the same jurisdiction/domain at the moment opposition binds?
pivot_observable: Public record (filings, press, lab announcements) of whether the lab named in the first pressure-driven reversal has an active or announced deployment of its own in that jurisdiction/domain versus operating only through third-party deployers/infrastructure partners there
pivot_because: This is the one variable the minutes show actually reordering the outcome set rather than just shifting confidence. If yes, the lab becomes the visible target and pre-emptively pulls its own API/feature from a downstream deployer's use case (ai-pressure and lab-moves' scenario, checkable by 2026-11-16). If no, the lab has no proximate exposure to absorb, so pressure lands on the hyperscaler/utility instead, producing a siting-restriction path (ai-public-backlash's scenario, checkable by 2026-11-03). These are materially different worlds — different named actor, different remedy type, different downstream rule layer — not just different odds on the same outcome. Fault attribution, by contrast, is asserted by most minutes to stop gating anything on this branch, so resolving it doesn't move the outcome set.
rival_pivots_rejected: ai-incident-severity's pivot (whether the reversal gets a published root-cause/mechanism finding vs. mere attribution language) does not reorder the outcome set: the minutes on both sides of the target question agree the reversal closes without a structural finding either way, so this variable shifts how the event is narrated, not who it targets or what remedy follows. ai-regulation-teeth's pivot (whether opposition retrofits teeth into developer-layer rules like SB 53/EU GPAI Code) is downstream of the target question, not independent of it — which layer gets codified follows from which entity absorbed the blame, so it's a consequence of the real pivot, not a rival to it.
ruling: The reversal's target is set by whether the implicated lab still has its own exposed deployment in that jurisdiction: if so, the lab pre-emptively pulls its own API/feature from a named deployer by 2026-11-16 and model-layer rules stay theatre; if not, an operator/infrastructure target absorbs the pressure and a state siting law follows by 2026-11-03, with new teeth codifying at the deployment layer either way.
because: pressure-model's REVISE explicitly overrides both the carried fault-layer fork and its own round-1 claim of a fixed operator target, replacing them with a conditional keyed to which entity's next choice moves the stakes — that conditional is the only mechanism in the minutes that can produce either ai-pressure/lab-moves' lab-centered scenario or ai-public-backlash's operator-centered scenario as a function of an observable prior state (the lab's existing exposure), rather than asserting one outcome as fixed. ai-incident-severity and ai-regulation-teeth both operate on axes (fault-finding, rule-layer codification) that the minutes treat as downstream of, or orthogonal to, that targeting question.
threat_live: Exposure decouples from causation: whichever entity is the visible face of the deployment absorbs blame and is compelled to act regardless of where technical fault actually lies, so a lab with no proximate deployment in the flashpoint jurisdiction becomes insulated even if its model caused the harm, while an operator or a lab with local exposure eats the consequence for a failure it may not have caused. The correlate risk: whatever concessions get extracted this way become the template regulators codify, so deployment-layer rules gain real teeth while model-layer rules (SB 53, EU GPAI Code) stay theatre unless opposition explicitly names the model layer.
strongest_minute: ai-incident-severity — its REVISE draws a precise, falsifiable distinction between attribution (accepting responsibility for handling) and mechanism (a named reproducible failure pattern), and predicts the two decouple in the first reversal. It's a sharp, checkable claim even though it doesn't bear on the pivot.
weakest_minute: ai-public-backlash — it needs not just a reversal landing on infrastructure but a specific enacted state siting law in force by a fixed near-term date, which is a much narrower and more specific compound outcome than the branch it's arguing from actually guarantees.
shared_assumption: ai-incident-severity, ai-regulation-teeth, lab-moves, and pressure-model (in its retained portion) all rely on 'binding public opposition severs the developer/operator fault-layer fork' without independently arguing for it — pressure-model states the mechanism, the other three just build on the conclusion. Treat this as one argument, not three or four independent confirmations.
smuggled_assumption: ai-public-backlash's claim requires a state-level siting restriction already 'enacted' and 'in force' by 2026-11-03 — the brief grants only that pressure operates 'without any court, agency, or state law yet requiring it' at the point of reversal; asserting a specific enacted statute on a fixed near-term date is an added premise about legislative speed, not a consequence drawn from the granted branch.
unresolved: Whether the first visible reversal (Stage 2's trigger event) has already occurred as of this writing, and if so which entity it named — the minutes argue the downstream target conditionally but none states the actual current exposure position of any specific named lab, so the pivot is well-defined but not yet resolved by anything in the record.
